summary: Mars Survival Guide is an offline, onboard map for a crewed mission in western Candor Chasma, Valles Marineris. It picks a safe landing site, finds the nearest water-bearing deposit, plans the safest route over real slope data and gives the crew a GO / CAUTION / NO-GO decision for the full round trip. On Mars there is no GPS, no internet and no rescue, so the crew must decide alone: our map answers "can we reach the water and still get home?"
details:
Slope layers built in QGIS from NASA MOLA elevation data are intersected with a grid of 5.6 million 100 m cells (237 × 237 km). Each passable cell becomes a node of a graph linked to its 8 neighbours, and an A* search finds the route: safe terrain first; medium slopes, chaotic terrain and a 500 m rockfall band along the walls are allowed only if no safe path exists. Steep slopes are never crossed. The mission check covers outbound + 2 h sampling + return: it says NO-GO if battery or oxygen run out, if the crew could not walk back within the 8 h suit limit should the rover fail, if the route climbs more than 1,000 m (a canyon wall) or if it exceeds ~12 h of daylight. The interface is dark, minimal and keyboard-first, and the whole app runs offline in a browser. Built with JavaScript, Leaflet, QGIS, Python (shapely) and Node.js; routes verified against a reference Dijkstra (25/25 identical) and 22 automated tests.

Full pitch video (1:15, English subtitles): https://youtu.be/9SJvCt2M5HY
